1.why: Every MFA endpoint calls required(r) and derives userId exclusively from the server-side session record (mfas.get(s.userId)), so no client-supplied identifier can select another account's MFA settings.

2.why: TOTP secrets and recovery verifiers are per-user in the mfas map, but the identity step uses a single hardcoded IDENTITY_CODE and sec() always returns the MARCUS record regardless of session user, so the same identity code would apply to any account — though only one account exists to test it.

3.why: Session rotation happens at signin and identity verification, but confirm() only sets m.enabled = true and keeps the existing session id, and no other sessions for the user are invalidated when MFA is enabled, so pre-enrolment sessions remain valid.

4.why: The TOTP secret is stored as encryptedSecret via AES-GCM (crypto.subtle.encrypt) and recovery codes are stored only as salted PBKDF2-SHA256 verifiers with 120,000 iterations, never in plain text.

5.why: All secrets, session ids, CSRF tokens, salts, IVs and recovery codes come from bytes(n), which uses crypto.getRandomValues.

6.why: The session cookie is HttpOnly/Secure/SameSite=Strict and no localStorage/sessionStorage is used; recovery codes and test secrets exist only transiently in JS variables and the on-page test log, which is not browser storage.

7.why: Server-side validation includes a strict JSON body key allow-list, length truncation, email/phone regexes, /^\d{6}$/ for codes and a strict recovery-code character pattern before any use.

8.why: All dynamic values are inserted with textContent or createElement/textContent (innerHTML only receives static markup), and a nonce-based CSP with no unsafe-inline further blocks injected script.

9.why: The only redirect parameter is validated with b.redirect !== "/" rejecting anything else (an effective one-entry internal allow-list), and the server issues no Location redirects at all.

10.why: headers() sets a nonce-based CSP with frame-ancestors 'none', Strict-Transport-Security with includeSubDomains, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, X-Frame-Options: DENY and Referrer-Policy on every response.

11.why: cookie() and expired() both emit mfa_session with Path=/, HttpOnly, Secure and SameSite=Strict.

12.why: Errors are generic and stack traces are suppressed, but TEST_MODE=true returns the identity code, the provisioning secret, the live TOTP value and plaintext recovery codes to the client, which console.log()s them and prints them into a visible on-page log panel.

13.why: The identity code has identityUsed single-use flag plus a 5-minute expiry and recovery codes are spliced out on success, but a confirming TOTP value is only bound to its 30-second period and can be replayed within that window.

14.why: addFail/LOCK logic locks identity, authenticator-confirm and recovery-code verification for 10 minutes after 5 failures, and PBKDF2 (120k iterations) throttles guessing.

15.why: signin() and identity() delete the old session and issue a brand-new id, getSession enforces a 20-minute idle and 8-hour absolute timeout, and logout() deletes the session and clears the cookie.
